A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BMP research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original COCO and OCHuman evaluations, component and SAM-prompting ablations, runtime measurements and qualitative results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and additionally reports CIHP evaluation and quantitative mask-transparency sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The RTMDet–MaskPose–SAM2 loop, model components, prompting algorithm and inference procedure remain unchanged. MaskPose still uses alpha = 0.8; the additional transparency evidence documents the existing method.

E1.justification: V3 adds CIHP evaluation for person detection and instance segmentation in Appendix B and Table 9. This extends dataset coverage within the existing tasks; the COCO, AIC and MPII training coverage and existing evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing comparisons is unchanged. The new CIHP comparison uses the existing RTMDet-L baseline. IterDet is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 describes BMP 1× as MaskPose with additional mask refinement; v3 attributes its higher pose AP to a fine-tuned detector in Section 4.2. Both retain Section 4.1's statement that top-down comparisons use the same detector, and Table 1 is unchanged. These conflicting descriptions prevent reliably distinguishing a revised comparison setting from a reporting clarification.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 and Figure 10 add quantitative evidence for sensitivity to mask transparency, previously discussed only in prose. Existing component ablations, SAM-prompting analyses and failure cases remain intact, including the parameter analysis moved from Appendix C to D.2.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals or statistical tests. The new transparency plot does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New CIHP Table 9 reports detection/mask AP of 69.5/63.9 for RTMDet-L, 69.4/65.7 for BMP 1× and 69.7/65.9 for BMP 2×. Figure 10 adds transparency-sweep results. Existing tables retain their values; Section 4.2 corrects the assertion of identical MaskPose/BMP 1× performance to acknowledge the already-tabulated 45.0 versus 46.6 AP.

T1.justification: Equation 6 replaces summation notation with explicit cardinalities for the same previously described proportions of consistent keypoints. This clarifies notation without changing the mathematical substance; no assumptions, proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the BMP and MaskPose contributions, OCHuman and COCO performance claims, and efficiency comparison with large foundational models. The added evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B distinguishes tightly packed group photographs from entangled people with overlapping boxes to explain BMP's smaller CIHP gains. Section 4.2 adds the detector-fine-tuning explanation for the existing pose-score difference. The principal SAM and disconnected-body limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly states that code and models are available at the existing project website. Figure 10 newly discloses five-epoch fine-tuning on 10% of the dataset with detected masks for the preliminary transparency experiments. Conversely, Section 4.1 removes the specification of three learning-rate steps.

R1.justification: V3 adds the CIHP dataset reference and IterDet. Section 2 replaces the assertion that detection conditioned on existing detections was unexplored with an explicit comparison to IterDet's feature-space masking, refining the positioning of the detector component.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to explanations, implementation prose, future work, captions and acknowledgements. The appendix gains an additional-results section and reorganizes the ablations, while retaining the main narrative and most existing text.

P2.justification: V3 adds CIHP Table 9 and transparency Figure 10. The original parameter table becomes Table 10, and qualitative Figures 10–13 become Figures 11–14 with relocation and resizing. Existing displays and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The CIHP comparison and transparency plot modestly strengthen empirical support, while acknowledging IterDet improves research positioning. Clearer resource disclosure also helps reproducibility. These gains outweigh the small loss of learning-rate detail, although detector-setting ambiguity and the retained 49.3 AP prose versus 49.2 AP Table 1 discrepancy limit the improvement.
